cards.b: System software runs and maintains the computer (OS, drivers, utilities). Application software lets the user do a task (word processor, browser).
System software that manages the computer's hardware and software and provides an interface for the user.
User interface, managing files, memory, peripherals and drivers, multitasking, security, user accounts, handling interrupts.
Software that lets the operating system communicate with and control a hardware device such as a printer.
A signal sent to the processor by hardware or software asking for immediate attention.
A key pressed or mouse clicked, printer out of paper, disk transfer finished, power failure.
Division by zero, two programs trying to use the same memory, an invalid instruction.
Checked at the end of each FDE cycle; if its priority is high enough, save the state; run the ISR; restore the state; resume.
The program that is run to deal with a particular interrupt.
Close to human language, portable between computers, easier to read and debug. Needs a compiler or interpreter.
Machine code or assembly language. Machine dependent, but gives direct control of hardware and efficient code.
Machine code is binary and the only language the CPU runs directly. Assembly uses mnemonics and needs an assembler.
Translates the whole source code into machine code (an executable file) before it is run. Reports all errors at the end.
Translates and runs the source code one line at a time. Stops at the first error. No executable file is produced.
Code editor with syntax highlighting, auto-completion and pretty-print; built-in translator; error diagnostics; breakpoints and variable watch.

gaps.s: The program that deals with a particular interrupt is called the interrupt ___ routine.
A ___ driver lets the operating system communicate with a printer.
Language that uses mnemonics such as ADD and LDA is called ___ language.
The only language the CPU can run directly is ___ code.
A ___ translates the whole program into an executable file before it is run.
An ___ translates and runs a program one line at a time.
Colouring keywords in the code editor is called syntax ___.
Before running an ISR, the CPU saves the current ___.

short.q: Describe two functions of an operating system.
short.model: Managing files: creating, moving, deleting and organising files and folders. Managing memory: allocating RAM to programs so they do not overwrite each other.

short.q: Describe what happens when a hardware interrupt is sent to the CPU while it runs a program.
short.model: At the end of the FDE cycle the CPU checks the interrupt's priority. If it is higher than the current task, the CPU saves its state, runs the ISR, then restores the state and resumes the program.
points: checked at end of FDE cycle / priority compared
state restored and original program resumes

short.q: Explain why interrupts are given priorities.
short.model: Some interrupts are more urgent than others, such as a power failure compared with a key press. The CPU only stops the current task for a higher priority interrupt; others wait.
points: only higher priority interrupts stop the current task

short.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of writing a washing machine program in a low-level language.
short.model: Advantage: direct control of the hardware, efficient small code. Disadvantage: harder to write and debug, and only works on one type of processor.

short.q: A programmer releases a finished game to customers. Explain why a compiler is better than an interpreter.
short.model: A compiler produces an executable file, so the game runs faster, customers do not need the translator, and the source code stays private.
points: no translator needed / source code kept private
